messages:
Anya P: Quick heads-up — reproducible divergence between fp16 and int4 (q3f) on long-prefill runs. Same prompt, same random seed, completions differ after ~12.2k tokens.
Miguel: Can you paste a tiny repro + logs?
Anya P: Repro steps (short):
```
# run on canary int4 build
export MODEL=magnet-13b-q3f
./run_infer --prefill-file long_demo.txt --max-tokens 4000 --dump-kv-checksum pre/post
```
Log excerpt: 
```
[2023-10-28T13:45:01Z] PREFILL len=14352 shards=4 kv_index_end=12288
[2023-10-28T13:45:02Z] EVICT prefix_window=8192 -> evict_range(4096,8191)
[2023-10-28T13:45:02Z] KV_CHECKSUM pre=0x7a1f2b89 post=0x9c4d3e01 mismatch
[2023-10-28T13:45:02Z] TOKEN_FLIP at pos=12290 expected="," got="."
```
I also tried disabling prefix caching (`--cache-prefix=false`) and divergence disappears.
Sasha: @Anya P can you run with KV_DEBUG=1 + `--dump-kv-entries 12280-12295` so we can diff keys?
Anya P: Running now, attaching diff snapshot below (trimmed):
```
# kv entry dump int4 vs fp16 at indices 12288..12292
int4:  kv_key(12288)=0x1b2c3d4e kv_val_hash=0x5a6b7c8d
fp16:  kv_key(12288)=0x1b2c3d4f kv_val_hash=0x5a6b7c8d
```
Only LSB differs in key mapping. Looks like phase/rope scaling mapping shifted by 1 for int4 path.
Samir: That rings a bell — we saw something similar during quant bring-up where rotary rescale got applied before the quantized kernel's index normalization. If shard boundary aligns with an eviction, the rounding path can flip.
Miguel: Hypothesis: quant kernels truncate low precision then `rope_scale(position)` rounding leads to off-by-one mapping when `kv_index % rotary_period == 0` and after evict+reinsert on warmstart.
Sasha: Quick mitigation: add a tiny epsilon when computing the discrete index in the int4 path: `idx = floor(pos*scale + 1e-6)` vs current `floor(pos*scale)`. Can you test `--force-rope-epsilon=1e-6`?
Anya P: Tested: with epsilon=1e-6, int4 keys align with fp16 and completions match for the sample. Perf overhead negligible.
Miguel: Good. What's the impact across heavy batches? Any regression in latency or token cost?
Anya P: Microbench: 3% CPU overhead on kernel launch, p50 latency +4ms on short sequences, p99 unchanged for long runs. Cost wise negligible.
Samir: We should add unit/regression tests: priming across boundary tokens [8191..8194], compare kv checksums across quant modes and fp16. Also add a fuzz that randomly evicts/rewrites keys across shards.
Miguel: I'll open INF ticket and schedule a canary patch. INF-3421 filed: "kv-index rope-scaling epsilon needed for quant kernels".
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: canary/2023-10-28-14:22 (2 nodes) — rolling patch `rope-epsilon-quant-fix`
Sasha: Also flag for model onboarding checklist: add long-prefill edgecase (>=12k tokens) to onboarding smoke for quantized variants. We keep seeing regressions only when longprefill + shard-evict happens.
Anya P: Agreed. I've added a short test harness and a golden set to the repo: `tests/long_prefill/goldens/magnet13b/`. PR coming.
Miguel: Thanks. Next steps: 1) merge epsilon fix behind flag, 2) add unit + fuzz tests, 3) run full quant-bench across 5 seeds and longprefill corpus, 4) roll to prod if stable.
Samir: Optional: look into whether rotary scaling should be integer-stable transform (avoid fp trunc rounding differences across kernels). Might be a longer refactor.
Anya P: Will attach sample deltas and short audio clip of the prompt failing (for product team). For now patch+smoke seems to resolve. :thumbsup:
Miguel: Cheers — let's keep the canary for 24h and monitor `kv-checksum-mismatch` metric. @Sasha will you own the tests?
Sasha: Yep, I'll add tests and the fuzz job.
Anya P: Posted the quick repro gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abcd1234 — contains commands and minimal longprefill.
Miguel: Good job team. :eyes:
